title: In 1920 the New York Times mocked Goddard’s rockets; it printed a correction in 1969

cover.alt: Black-and-white film still of a small rocket firing a bright jet of flame inside a tall open metal launching tower in a field, beside a bare tree.
cover.credit: US Air Force film of Robert H. Goddard’s tests · Public domain

body: In January 1920 an unsigned *New York Times* editorial scoffed at Robert Goddard’s idea of a rocket reaching beyond the atmosphere, arguing that once it left the air its charges could no longer drive it forward. Goddard had already shown in lab tests that a rocket needs no air to push against, and works even more efficiently in a vacuum. He went on to launch the world’s first liquid-fuelled rocket on 16 March 1926. On 17 July 1969, the day after Apollo 11 lifted off for the Moon, the *Times* printed ‘A Correction’ and said it regretted the error.

slides.alt: Black-and-white film of Goddard’s early tests: a small rocket hangs inside a tall open launching tower in a field and fires a jet of flame and sparks downward; in a second test the flame burns brighter.
slides.caption: Massachusetts, 1928: one of Robert Goddard’s liquid-fuelled rockets fires inside its launching tower, from a US Air Force film history of his tests.
slides.credit: US Air Force · Public domain · excerpt

slides.text: Of course, [Goddard] only seems to lack the knowledge ladled out daily in high schools.
slides.attribution: Unsigned New York Times editorial, 13 January 1920

slides.question: Goddard’s first liquid-fuelled rocket, in 1926, climbed how high?
slides.explanation: Just 41 feet (12.5 m), in a 2.5-second flight that ended 184 feet away in a cabbage field. Still, it showed liquid fuels could power a rocket.

slides.text: Further investigation and experimentation have confirmed the findings of Isaac Newton in the 17th Century and it is now definitely established that a rocket can function in a vacuum as well as in an atmosphere. The Times regrets the error.
slides.attribution: The New York Times, ‘A Correction’, 17 July 1969
